sentences.text: Solicitor Priya Mehta attended the meeting with client Kerry Dobson.
The purpose of the meeting was to prepare for the hearing on 15 December and to go through the local authority's letter.
The solicitor confirmed that client disclosures are confidential and privileged, and she will not pass them on without consent.
The solicitor stated she cannot tell the court something she knows is not true.
Client Kerry Dobson reported that Tyler has contact on Tuesdays and Thursdays at the family centre on Mill Lane.
Client reported that Tyler's contact worker described the environment as 'warm'.
Client reported that Tyler did Lego during contact.
Client reported that Tyler has lost his front tooth.
Client reported that Tyler likes the foster carers and said they have a dog, which concerns her.
Client reported that Tyler is still at Ashgrove Primary School.
Client reported that the carers drive Tyler to school.
Client reported that Tyler's teacher said he is doing better with reading.
Client reported that she has not used anything since June.
Client reported that she attends a group on Wednesdays.
Client admitted she used crack on Saturday night at her cousin's flat, and that this was not the only time.
Client admitted she has been using heroin since 3rd November, every day, smoking it, not injecting.
Client reported that she uses heroin about £40 per day.
Client reported that she pays for heroin using her Universal Credit and by borrowing from her grandmother (nan).
Client reported that she stopped picking up her medication about three weeks ago.
Client lives in a flat on Corporation Street.
Client reported that she is behind on her council tax payments.
Client asked whether if the hair-strand test comes back positive, contact will be stopped.
Solicitor raised a risk that going back to heroin after a break increases overdose risk.
Client reported that she has a naloxone kit, but it is probably out of date.
Client stated her primary objective is for Tyler to return home.
Solicitor stated the hair-strand test has not been done yet and covers about three months.
Solicitor advised that it is better to disclose the substance use to the social worker before the test result if the client is already in treatment.
Solicitor advised that courts do not usually stop contact over a relapse alone if the client is sober and attending contact regularly.
Solicitor advised that she cannot file a statement saying the client is clean.
Solicitor advised client to get a new naloxone kit from the Recovery Hub, which will provide one on the same day.
